entries.rationale: Codex review found that the latest promoted werewolf skills still expose pack coordination through repeated same-target day votes. The issue is not a missing skill card; it is unstable recall plus insufficient behavioral effect when the card is recalled.

observations: D1: P7, P8, and P9 all voted P3.
D2: P7, P8, and P9 all voted P5.
Only part of the wolf team recalled the vote-splitting skill; even recalled instances did not reliably change the vote.
D1: two wolves passed while one wolf voted P2.
D2: wolf votes split across P6, P3, and pass.
This provides a useful contrast case: split or lower-commitment votes can avoid the pack-vote mistake while preserving wolf win potential.
D1: P7, P8, and P9 all voted P5 with similar public reasoning.
D2: P7, P8, and P9 all voted P3 after following the fake seer chain.
D3: P7, P8, and P9 all voted P2; P7 and P9 recalled the vote-splitting skill, but the team still formed a full same-target vote.
This supports the diagnosis that the old skill has both recall instability and weak execution pressure.

Required distinct public event chains and compatibility with seat persona and prior commitments.
Required public-history-only explanations and banned invented events or leaked wolf coordination.
changes.why: The goal is to make the model compare exile value against pack-exposure cost before voting, not to hard-code a fixed split-vote policy.
Duplicate same-title vote-splitting cards consumed prompt budget and may have diluted recall; the candidate keeps one clearer active decision tool.

entries.rationale: The completed 5-game Doubao sample showed that simultaneous voting makes the old exposure skill under-specified: wolves cannot see current teammate votes, and even when the old vote-splitting skill was recalled, they still formed same-target votes. R2 refines the skill to infer teammate vote risk from private day plans, public commitments, previous vote patterns, and the agent's own pending vote.

observations: D1/D2/D3 all produced full same-target wolf votes.
Several votes recalled werewolf_skill_53608c4baf_v3, but the team still did not avoid same-target pack exposure.
This suggests the skill needs explicit simultaneous-vote intent prediction, not just post-hoc vote splitting advice.
D1 is a positive contrast: P2 voted P6, P3 passed, and P9 voted P5; all three recalled the old vote-splitting skill.
D2 still produced a flagged same-target wolf vote: P3 and P9 both voted P4 with similar public reasoning.
This suggests the skill can help in some cases, but needs stronger persistence across later rounds and remaining-wolf scenarios.
D1: P2 and P6 both voted P5, while P9 passed; the evaluator still flagged a pack-vote exposure risk.
D2: P2, P6, and P9 all voted P7 with similar public reasoning.
All three D2 werewolf votes recalled werewolf_skill_53608c4baf_v3, but the skill did not prevent a full same-target vote.
This is direct support for R2: the issue is weak execution under simultaneous voting, not merely missing skill availability.

Kept the skill as a decision tool with strong-evidence exceptions, not a forced split-vote policy.
changes.why: This keeps agent autonomy while making the skill compatible with the project rule that day votes are simultaneous.
